answer: Operator rule: cap two identities per network origin (ASN), verified by independent route checks against a public beacon feed. Each identity locks 50 units, forfeited if its origin is spoofed or shared. One fake costs 50 units and one clean ASN; ten fakes need five ASNs and 500 units, and each extra ASN costs more to rent, so cost rises faster than count. No operator climbs to the summit of throughput by stacking identities on one network, and the zenith of full quota requires distinct origins plus audited work.
